at-a-glance.item: No wages does not establish zero countable healthcare income
at-a-glance.detail: DHCS lists taxable interest and taxable rental income as countable MAGI items; IRS rental rules determine allowable expenses. CFTC exchange status does not establish Kalshi tax characterization or this person's realized amount.
at-a-glance.flag: The individual's tax character, household size and actual countable monthly/annual amounts are unknown. Do not treat deposits or gross payouts as verified income.

at-a-glance.item: 2026 one-person MAGI Medi-Cal income reference (not a personal finding)
at-a-glance.detail: California publishes these figures for a one-person household for 2026. Whether a particular adult qualifies depends on actual household and other eligibility facts; 2027 Medi-Cal FPL is not established here.

at-a-glance.item: New federal law: Medicaid "community engagement" (work) requirement begins January 1, 2027
at-a-glance.value: 80 hours/month, or $580 income, or an exemption
at-a-glance.detail: Section 71119 of H.R. 1 (Public Law 119-21) requires states to condition Medicaid eligibility on community engagement for certain adults ages 19–64. California has already written this into state law: AB 2161 (Chapter 209, Statutes of 2026) amended Welfare and Institutions Code § 14005.69.

at-a-glance.item: The $580 test does not require earned income
at-a-glance.value: $580 total monthly MAGI-based household income; no wages-only gate
at-a-glance.detail: California Welfare & Institutions Code §14005.69(e)(6) uses MAGI-based financial methods for the household. DHCS's member notice says income "from any source"; earlier county guidance uses "gross" but was preliminary. Averaging under §(e)(7) is reserved for seasonal workers; actual qualification is unknown.

decision.item: If otherwise eligible: 2026 MAGI Medi-Cal one-person 138% limit
decision.detail: MAGI Medi-Cal may be available without wages or a property limit in the applicable group; no individual eligibility is assumed. Work rule starts Jan 2027 for affected adults; six-month financial eligibility checks begin Mar 2027.

decision.item: Marketplace plan: federal premium help only if all criteria are met
decision.detail: Different FPL reference years apply. Annual household MAGI and other IRS tax-credit eligibility conditions control; no automatic APTC throughout a 138–400% band. 2027 state premium assistance extends to 200% FPL ($31,920 one person) for eligible enrollees.

decision.item: Marketplace plan above the applicable plan-year subsidy reference
decision.value: Plan-specific full-price quote — not available here
decision.detail: The 2026 one-person marketplace 400% FPL reference is $62,600; 2027 is $63,840. A plan can be purchased subject to enrollment rules, but a personal quote is not provided by the FPL chart.

decision.item: Income below marketplace 100% FPL, or Medicaid unavailable for other reasons
decision.value: Medi-Cal screening; exceptions to the federal PTC floor can apply
decision.detail: A zero/low-income applicant is not automatically in an expansion aid code. IRS lists special circumstances below 100% FPL; why Medicaid is unavailable matters, especially a community-engagement failure.

decision.item: Marketplace assistance after other Medi-Cal ineligibility
decision.detail: The 2027 FPL chart shows percentages for eligible applicants, not a guarantee for everyone denied Medi-Cal. DHCS warns of lost marketplace help after work-rule disqualification.
decision.flag: No blanket 0%-premium marketplace fallback exists. Work-rule Medicaid disqualification may bar Covered California financial assistance; personal outcome depends on the reason for denial and all IRS/marketplace criteria.

work-summary.value: Adults 19–64 in the MAGI New Adult Group
work-summary.detail: California applies the rule to the MAGI New Adult Group (aid code M1) — adults 19 to 64 with income up to 138% FPL — and to state-funded Medi-Cal adults who meet the same criteria. It applies regardless of immigration status.

work-summary.item: Who the rule does not cover
work-summary.value: Non-MAGI groups, children's group, pregnancy group, restricted-scope (emergency) Medi-Cal
work-summary.detail: Members covered under other Medi-Cal groups such as Non-MAGI programs, the Mandatory Children's Group or the Pregnancy Group are excluded from work and community engagement requirements.

work-summary.value: $580 monthly MAGI-based household income; seasonal averaging only for seasonal workers
work-summary.detail: At application the previous month is assessed; at redetermination, a month since the previous determination. California §14005.69(e)(6)–(7) limits the prior-six-month average to seasonal workers. The individual's countable amount is unknown.

work-summary.value: 80 hours in a month of work, volunteering, community service, or a work program
work-summary.detail: A combined 80 hours works: "Work at any kind of job, volunteer, do community service, or attend a job-training program for a combined total of at least 80 hours in any month since your last renewal."

work-summary.value: Enrolled at least half-time in a qualifying program
work-summary.detail: The statutory half-time enrollment alternative depends on program rules. Do not equate plain-language "part time" with every part-time credit load.

work-summary.value: 13 categories of specified excluded individuals plus 4 hardship categories
work-summary.detail: Full lists on the Work rules page.

work-summary.value: Preceding month at application; any month since determination at redetermination
work-summary.detail: The two work-rule look-backs differ. DHCS dates the new six-month financial eligibility checks to March 1, 2027; the work-rule start is January 1, 2027.

work-summary.value: 30-day notice, coverage continues during the 30 days, then loss of Medi-Cal — and no Covered California financial help
work-summary.detail: The county must first check every other basis of eligibility before denying, and must give written notice and a state hearing opportunity.
